[[Ukanomitama|Tamahime-no-Mikoto]] (Hime no MIya)|website=http://kikuko-nagoya.com/html/ooagata-shrine.html}} Ōagata Shrine (大縣神社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Inuyama, Aichi, Japan[[Aichi Prefecture|.]] It was recorded in the [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] as a [[Myojin Taisha]]. It is the [[Ninomiya]] or second ranked shrine of [[Owari Province]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]]. It is located next to {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}}. A shrine famous for its Harvest Festival [[Hōnensai]], or the penis festival held annually on March 15.https://www.e-periodica.ch/cntmng?pid=act-001%3A1959%3A16%3A%3A995{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5isFdtMGwVwC&dq=tagata+shrine&pg=PA246|title=Women in Myth|last=Knapp|first=Bettina L.|date=1997-01-01|publisher=SUNY Press|isbn=978-0-7914-3164-1|language=en}} It has a vagina festival on May 14th. Their festival is more subdued.{{Cite web|title=Hime-no-miya Matsuri in Inuyama 犬山の姫の宮祭り by Matthew Haswell|url=https://pbase.com/xerius/himenomiya|access-date=2024-04-08|website=PBase|language=en-US}} They demonstrate religious traditions that starkly contrast with the conventional Western views, on sexuality. With the {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} it is renowned for hosting festivals that prominently showcase sexual symbols showcasing Japans open and accepting attitude towards sexual themes.https://brill.com/previewpdf/book/9789004293786/B9789004293786_003.xml Its name literally means large territory or large [[prefecture]] shrine. The kanji 縣 is the older form of the kanji for prefecture. There are many {{ill|Agata Shrine|ja|縣神社|lt=Agata Shrines}} with the same kanji 縣神社. [[Tagata Shrine]] also has a similar name with the kanji 田 Ta (farm) at the front rather than Great 大 {{clear}} ==Overview== [[File:Oagata1.jpg|thumb| torii gate]] It is the [[Ichinomiya|Ninomiya]], or a second ranked shrine in [[Owari Province]], ranked below {{ill|Masumida Shrine|en}}..{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher=Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} It is located close to {{ill|Tagata Shrine|simple}} the shrine famous for hosting [[Hōnensai]]. Oagata shrine has a similar yonic festival the Sunday before this festival{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2012-03-24 |title=Fertility festival (Oh-agata/ Oagata Jinja) |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2012/03/24/hime-no-miya-festival-ogata-jinja/ |access-date=2023-04-27 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}} [[Aotsuka Kofun]] is located on the grounds of the shrine, 3.5 kilometers to the west of the [[honden]]. The shrine claims that the ''[[kofun]]'' is the grave of its ''[[kami]]'', {{nihongo|Oarata-no-mikoto|大荒田命||}}. During the [[Sengoku period]], the tumulus was fortified as a castle by the forces of [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] during the 1584 {{ill|Battle of Komaki and Nagakute|en}}.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}} {{in lang|ja}} The annual Good Harvest Festival, also known as the Hime no Miya Hōnen Festival is celebrated at Ōagata Shrine, in Inuyama, Aichi, Japan. This special event occurs on nearest Sunday to March 15th each year. Is well known for its emphasis on fertility and prosperity especially representing symbolism. It serves as a celebration to the Good Harvest Festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} creating an observance of fertility with both male and female representations.{{Cite web|date=2008-10-13|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Individual Shrine Observances : Hōnen matsuri|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081013022700/http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=973|access-date=2024-04-08|website=web.archive.org}}{{Cite web|last=Greve|first=Gabi|date=2009-05-15|title=Honen Matsuri Harvest Festival|url=https://wkdfestivalsaijiki.blogspot.com/2009/05/honen-matsuri-harvest-festival.html|access-date=2024-04-08|website=WKD - Saijiki for Festivals and Ceremonies}} The Oagata Shrine, situated in the Owari region holds importance as a Shinto shrine dedicated to Oagata no okami a deity revered for cultivating the Owari area. Known as the prominent shrine, in Owari, Oagata no okami is highly respected as a protective guardian bringing prosperity to businesses and safeguarding against misfortune.{{Cite web|title=Oagata Shrine｜Inuyama Cultural Heritage Navi|url=https://inuyama-tabi.com/en/point/detail/233/|access-date=2024-04-08|website=inuyama-tabi.com}} The Oagata Shrine, located in Inuyama City, within Aichi Prefecture symbolizes Japans traditions by blending ancient customs with modern practices. It is renowned for its festivals that honor fertility and the equilibrium of female energies. Deeply rooted in spirituality this shrine complements the {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} creating a celebration of fertility through their annual events.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=5N8zDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA341&lpg=PA341&dq=%C5%8Cagata+Shrine&source=bl&ots=tWZ72Pe3r1&sig=ACfU3U2PRGcSzIHmkAFq3W8xGUAdo50gcg&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiLgMyErbOFAxUVCTQIHY2HBJE4FBDoAXoECAMQAw#v=onepage&q=%C5%8Cagata%20Shrine&f=false|title=Japan’s Sexual Gods: Shrines, Roles and Rituals of Procreation and Protection|last=Turnbull|first=Stephen|date=2015-05-19|publisher=BRILL|isbn=978-90-04-29378-6|language=en}}{{rp|331-353}} With its history, stunning architecture and distinctive cultural celebrations Oagata Shrine continues to play a role, in Japans spiritual and cultural landscape.{{rp|331-353}} The festivals held at the Oagata Shrine honor the elements of life, fertility and the balance, between female energies. These traditions not uphold Japans heritage but also provide a glimpse into how celebrations have adapted to modern times. The shrines longstanding significance symbolizes the enduring link, between people and spirituality connecting present and future generations.{{rp|331-353}} The Ōagata Shrine stands out as a known Shinto shrine situated in Inuyama, Aichi, Japan, Japan. It pays homage to the revered deity Ōagata oomikami, who is hailed as the trailblazer of the Owari region and a symbol of prosperity and good luck, in business endeavors. Locally referred to as Ninomiya meaning "the shrine " this sacred place holds significance for the community.{{Cite web|title=Kikuko's Website: Oagata Shrine/Honen-sai/|url=http://kikuko-nagoya.com/html/ooagata-shrine.html|access-date=2024-04-08|website=kikuko-nagoya.com}} == deity and Importance == At the heart of Ōagata Shrine lies Ōagata oomikami, honored for their pioneering contributions to Owari and association with prosperity. The shrine serves as a cultural hub in the area drawing visitors seeking blessings for success in business ventures. The shrine claims that the ''[[kofun]]'' is the grave of its ''[[kami]]'', {{nihongo|Oarata-no-mikoto|大荒田命||}}. During the [[Sengoku period]], the tumulus was fortified as a castle by the forces of [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] during the 1584 {{ill|Battle of Komaki and Nagakute|en}}. Enshrining Oagata no okami carries a legacy. Legend has it that the deity was initially enshrined on Mt. Hongu overlooking the Nobi Plain. In a relocation event dating back to 3 BCE, Oagata no okami was transferred to its shrine location solidifying its significance in the local religious context. Dedicated to Oagata no okami a deity associated with the development of the Owari region the Oagata Shrine holds a place as Owaris shrine. It serves as a space where worshippers seek blessings for prosperity and protection from adversity. The shrines history is highlighted by its relocation to its location in 3 BCE from Mt. Hongu showcasing its enduring importance in the communitys beliefs, throughout history.{{rp|331-353}} == Description == [[File:Oagata Shrine Hime no Miya Plum Orchard - 2018.jpg|thumb| Hime no Miya and Umezono]] [[File:Inuyama Oagata Plum Blossoms Over Shrine Rooftops.jpg|thumb| A plum orchard made on a slope.]] There are many small shrines within the precincts of Ogata Shrine. In the past, there used to be two Betsugu shrines and 52 subordinate shrines. One of these shrines, called Hime no Miya, is dedicated to Tamahime no Mikoto (although some people believe it is dedicated to Kurinama no kami). Since ancient times, this shrine has been worshipped as a guardian deity for safe childbirth. This is related to the phallus-shaped object at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} in Komaki City. At the top of Mt. Hongu, there is Hongu Shrine, which is dedicated to the Aramitama of Oogata no Okami. The building of the Ogata Shrine is known as 'Ogata-zukuri' and was constructed in 1661 by {{Ill|Mitsutomo Tokugawa|en}}, ruled the {{ill|Owari Domain|en}} succeeding his father. [http://ooagata.urdr.weblife.me/pg149.html 大縣神社について] In addition to the shrine itself, Ogata Shrine also oversees the [[Aotsuka Kofun]], which is the second largest {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en}} mound in [[Aichi Prefecture]]. The surrounding area is also filled with ancient burial mounds, including round burial mounds. On the slope of the mountain behind the shrine's grounds, there are approximately 300 weeping plum trees. === Architectural Style === The Oagata Shrine holds a place, in the hearts of the people not as a symbol of history and architectural beauty but also as a source of spiritual guidance for those seeking prosperity and protection. Its popularity among both locals and visitors from places highlights its importance as an spiritual hub. By honoring Oagata no okami the shrine maintains its role in the community fostering a connection to tradition and heritage. In essence the Oagata Shrine stands as a landmark that bridges the gap between past and present embodying both the legacy and architectural excellence of the Owari region. Its enduring relevance and the devotion it inspires reflect the impact of Shinto practices, on Japans cultural and religious tapestry. === 1661 restoration === In 1661 Tokugawa Mitsutomo, the lord of the [[Owari Tokugawa Clan]] (rulers of the Owari domain and a cadet branch of the Tokugawa clan, not to be confused with the [[Owari clan]] associated with [[Atsuta Shrine]]) oversaw the reconstruction of the shrine using Santoh zukuri or Ōagata zukuri architectural style. This distinctive construction method is deemed a asset nationally and showcases the unique Owari zukuri architectural heritage. The shrine premises maintain a representation of Owari zukuri aesthetics adding to its cultural significance. It uses {{ill|Owari-zukuri|en}} architecture.https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9696 The shrines existing hall meticulously restored in 1661 by Tokugawa Mitsutomo, the lord of the Owari Domain stands as a testament to the enduring traditions of the Owari region. This restoration work preserved the Owari zukuri building style now esteemed for its historical value. Recognized for its significance and contribution, to Japans heritage the shrine received national recognition as an important cultural property in 1981. Following a restoration led by Tokugawa Mitsutomo in 1661 the shrine boasts architecture reflecting the Owari zukuri construction style.Being recognized as a treasure in 1981 highlights the architectural and historical importance of the shrine preserving a crucial aspect of Japans rich cultural heritage.{{rp|331-353}} === Attractions and Special Sites === The Haiden, known as the Hall of Worship leads to the Honden the shrine recognized as a cultural asset. The shrine grounds also feature an "ema”, for couples seeking blessings for fertility.[[File:Ōagata-jinja_Himeishi.jpg|thumb|293x293px| Himeishi]]The Lady Stone. Hime ishi One striking element at the shrine is the Hime ishi, a stone resembling anatomy located near the Hime no miya shrine. This stone, along with yang stones, at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} collectively known as "in'yoh seki" or yin and yang stones represents fertility and creation. Plum Trees and Hime no miya Shrine [[File:大縣神社 神宮遙拝所 - 1.jpg|thumb|Jingu Yohaijo, or remote worship site for [[Ise Grand Shrine]]]] Surrounded by plum trees the shrine creates a tranquil and scenic atmosphere. Within its premises stands the Hime no miya Shrine dedicated to goddess Tamahime no mikoto. Visitors frequent this site to pray for childbirth, fertility, harmonious relationships and marital bliss. [[File:Small_shrine_of_Oagata-jinja_near_the_top_of_Mount_Hongu_-_3.jpg|thumb|Yama uba Shrine at the top of the mountain]] == Festival == The Hime no Miya Festival, which takes place around the time, as the fertility focused festivities at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} demonstrates the shrines commitment to fertility by honoring both female aspects. This festival, featuring processions and symbols depicting genitalia underscores the shrines connection to the cycles of life and abundance.{{rp|331-353}} The Oagata Shrine festival is sometimes called the Yin Festival, juxaposing it with the Yanf Festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}}. This is because Oagata Shrine celebrates female fertility (yin) and Tagata Shrine celebrates male fertility (yang). The festivities include rituals involving rocks symbolizing anatomy and a procession showcasing a palanquin (mi koshi) designed to resemble female genitalia. Alongside this palanquin visitors can witness banners (nobori) and adorned horses parading around the shrine grounds. A distinctive feature of this festival is the tradition of tossing luck mochi from a palanquin carrying a massive clam. Attendees eagerly gather near the shrine hall to catch these items and other treasures hanging from the sakaki tree. These artifacts are believed to possess powers offering blessings for safe childbirth prosperous marriages and contentment, in marital unions. The Rich Harvest Festival at Ōagata Shrine—also known as Hohnen sai—takes place annually in March. Holds a place, within the local community. The {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} Rich Harvest Festival complements the essence of fertility and abundance symbolizing values through rituals and festivities that attract visitors from all corners of the region. The parallel event held at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} in Komaki City, Aichi Prefecture commemorates the male fertility aspect on the occasion. This celebration is inspired by the tale of Takeinazumi no mikoto, a deity known for his phallus who wed Aratahime no mikoto a revered goddess. The highlight of {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} festivity is the procession featuring a palanquin carrying a linga (representing male genitalia) measuring nearly two meters long. It is followed by youths carrying a banner depicting a phallus. During the festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} attendees eagerly collect fragments of the banner as they believe these pieces hold properties that can ensure crops nurture harmonious relationships and guard against ailments related to intimacy. These fragments are traditionally placed in fields to promote prosperity. Both festivals have roots in customs and are cherished for their emphasis on fertility, abundance and the circle of life. They attract visitors from parts of Japan and beyond providing an enriching glimpse into cultural traditions linked to fertility rituals and reverence, for natural elements. Attending both the Yin festival, at Ōagata Shrine and the Yang festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} is believed to be important for receiving blessings in areas of life and prosperity. These festivals not mark the cycle and human fertility but also have a significant impact, on upholding and spreading local culture and traditions displaying the array of Japanese religious customs and beliefs. == Tourism == The presence of symbols in these shrines can elicit. Shock among foreign visitors a reaction that was more pronounced in earlier times. For instance a foreign traveler in 1970 was taken aback upon encountering symbols for the time, in a popular history magazine detailing these shrines annual festivities. The striking visual representation the banner showcased at the Oagata Festival portraying genitalia vividly illustrates the contrast, in sexual expressions between Japan and Western cultures. The initial shock experienced by travelers in the past has gradually diminished over time suggesting a decreasing disparity in attitudes towards sexuality. This transition is evidenced by the reception of exhibitions in the UK that delve into imagery from times showing a historical Western acceptance of sexual themes similar to contemporary Japanese views. Tourists participate in a variety of customs, such, as purifying themselves at the torii gate walking through a torii to show dedication and making wishes for their desires to be fulfilled. Throughout the years Oagata Shrine and its festivals have adapted to times by blending customs with present day perspectives. While some festival elements have changed or been reimagined to align with views on gender and sexuality the core theme of celebrating fertility and unity remains constant. These adjustments mirror a shift towards recognizing and respecting diverse expressions of human sexuality and fertility within their historical and cultural contexts.{{rp|331-353}} == Directions == To reach Ōagata Shrine ride the Meijo subway line, transfer at Heiandori station to the Kami iida line. The final stop is Gakuden station. From there it's a 1.5 km stroll to the shrine. [[Ukanomitama|Tamahime-no-Mikoto]] (Hime no MIya)|website=http://kikuko-nagoya.com/html/ooagata-shrine.html}} Ōagata Shrine (大縣神社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Inuyama, Aichi, Japan[[Aichi Prefecture|.]] It was recorded in the [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] as a [[Myojin Taisha]]. It is the [[Ninomiya]] or second ranked shrine of [[Owari Province]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]]. It is located next to {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}}. A shrine famous for its Harvest Festival [[Hōnensai]], or the penis festival held annually on March 15.https://www.e-periodica.ch/cntmng?pid=act-001%3A1959%3A16%3A%3A995{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5isFdtMGwVwC&dq=tagata+shrine&pg=PA246|title=Women in Myth|last=Knapp|first=Bettina L.|date=1997-01-01|publisher=SUNY Press|isbn=978-0-7914-3164-1|language=en}} It has a vagina festival on May 14th. Their festival is more subdued.{{Cite web|title=Hime-no-miya Matsuri in Inuyama 犬山の姫の宮祭り by Matthew Haswell|url=https://pbase.com/xerius/himenomiya|access-date=2024-04-08|website=PBase|language=en-US}} They demonstrate religious traditions that starkly contrast with the conventional Western views, on sexuality. With the {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} it is renowned for hosting festivals that prominently showcase sexual symbols showcasing Japans open and accepting attitude towards sexual themes.https://brill.com/previewpdf/book/9789004293786/B9789004293786_003.xml Its name literally means large territory or large [[prefecture]] shrine. The kanji 縣 is the older form of the kanji for prefecture. There are many {{ill|Agata Shrine|ja|縣神社|lt=Agata Shrines}} with the same kanji 縣神社. [[Tagata Shrine]] also has a similar name with the kanji 田 Ta (farm) at the front rather than Great 大 {{clear}} ==Overview== [[File:Oagata1.jpg|thumb| torii gate]] It is the [[Ichinomiya|Ninomiya]], or a second ranked shrine in [[Owari Province]], ranked below {{ill|Masumida Shrine|en}}..{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher=Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} It is located close to {{ill|Tagata Shrine|simple}} the shrine famous for hosting [[Hōnensai]]. Oagata shrine has a similar yonic festival the Sunday before this festival{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2012-03-24 |title=Fertility festival (Oh-agata/ Oagata Jinja) |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2012/03/24/hime-no-miya-festival-ogata-jinja/ |access-date=2023-04-27 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}} [[Aotsuka Kofun]] is located on the grounds of the shrine, 3.5 kilometers to the west of the [[honden]]. The shrine claims that the ''[[kofun]]'' is the grave of its ''[[kami]]'', {{nihongo|Oarata-no-mikoto|大荒田命||}}. During the [[Sengoku period]], the tumulus was fortified as a castle by the forces of [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] during the 1584 {{ill|Battle of Komaki and Nagakute|en}}.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}} {{in lang|ja}} The annual Good Harvest Festival, also known as the Hime no Miya Hōnen Festival is celebrated at Ōagata Shrine, in Inuyama, Aichi, Japan. This special event occurs on nearest Sunday to March 15th each year. Is well known for its emphasis on fertility and prosperity especially representing symbolism. It serves as a celebration to the Good Harvest Festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} creating an observance of fertility with both male and female representations.{{Cite web|date=2008-10-13|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Individual Shrine Observances : Hōnen matsuri|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081013022700/http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=973|access-date=2024-04-08|website=web.archive.org}}{{Cite web|last=Greve|first=Gabi|date=2009-05-15|title=Honen Matsuri Harvest Festival|url=https://wkdfestivalsaijiki.blogspot.com/2009/05/honen-matsuri-harvest-festival.html|access-date=2024-04-08|website=WKD - Saijiki for Festivals and Ceremonies}} The Oagata Shrine, situated in the Owari region holds importance as a Shinto shrine dedicated to Oagata no okami a deity revered for cultivating the Owari area. Known as the prominent shrine, in Owari, Oagata no okami is highly respected as a protective guardian bringing prosperity to businesses and safeguarding against misfortune.{{Cite web|title=Oagata Shrine｜Inuyama Cultural Heritage Navi|url=https://inuyama-tabi.com/en/point/detail/233/|access-date=2024-04-08|website=inuyama-tabi.com}} The Oagata Shrine, located in Inuyama City, within Aichi Prefecture symbolizes Japans traditions by blending ancient customs with modern practices. It is renowned for its festivals that honor fertility and the equilibrium of female energies. Deeply rooted in spirituality this shrine complements the {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} creating a celebration of fertility through their annual events.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=5N8zDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA341&lpg=PA341&dq=%C5%8Cagata+Shrine&source=bl&ots=tWZ72Pe3r1&sig=ACfU3U2PRGcSzIHmkAFq3W8xGUAdo50gcg&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiLgMyErbOFAxUVCTQIHY2HBJE4FBDoAXoECAMQAw#v=onepage&q=%C5%8Cagata%20Shrine&f=false|title=Japan’s Sexual Gods: Shrines, Roles and Rituals of Procreation and Protection|last=Turnbull|first=Stephen|date=2015-05-19|publisher=BRILL|isbn=978-90-04-29378-6|language=en}}{{rp|331-353}} With its history, stunning architecture and distinctive cultural celebrations Oagata Shrine continues to play a role, in Japans spiritual and cultural landscape.{{rp|331-353}} The festivals held at the Oagata Shrine honor the elements of life, fertility and the balance, between female energies. These traditions not uphold Japans heritage but also provide a glimpse into how celebrations have adapted to modern times. The shrines longstanding significance symbolizes the enduring link, between people and spirituality connecting present and future generations.{{rp|331-353}} The Ōagata Shrine stands out as a known Shinto shrine situated in Inuyama, Aichi, Japan, Japan. It pays homage to the revered deity Ōagata oomikami, who is hailed as the trailblazer of the Owari region and a symbol of prosperity and good luck, in business endeavors. Locally referred to as Ninomiya meaning "the shrine " this sacred place holds significance for the community.{{Cite web|title=Kikuko's Website: Oagata Shrine/Honen-sai/|url=http://kikuko-nagoya.com/html/ooagata-shrine.html|access-date=2024-04-08|website=kikuko-nagoya.com}} == deity and Importance == At the heart of Ōagata Shrine lies Ōagata oomikami, honored for their pioneering contributions to Owari and association with prosperity. The shrine serves as a cultural hub in the area drawing visitors seeking blessings for success in business ventures. The shrine claims that the ''[[kofun]]'' is the grave of its ''[[kami]]'', {{nihongo|Oarata-no-mikoto|大荒田命||}}. During the [[Sengoku period]], the tumulus was fortified as a castle by the forces of [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] during the 1584 {{ill|Battle of Komaki and Nagakute|en}}. Enshrining Oagata no okami carries a legacy. Legend has it that the deity was initially enshrined on Mt. Hongu overlooking the Nobi Plain. In a relocation event dating back to 3 BCE, Oagata no okami was transferred to its shrine location solidifying its significance in the local religious context. Dedicated to Oagata no okami a deity associated with the development of the Owari region the Oagata Shrine holds a place as Owaris shrine. It serves as a space where worshippers seek blessings for prosperity and protection from adversity. The shrines history is highlighted by its relocation to its location in 3 BCE from Mt. Hongu showcasing its enduring importance in the communitys beliefs, throughout history.{{rp|331-353}} == Description == [[File:Oagata Shrine Hime no Miya Plum Orchard - 2018.jpg|thumb| Hime no Miya and Umezono]] [[File:Inuyama Oagata Plum Blossoms Over Shrine Rooftops.jpg|thumb| A plum orchard made on a slope.]] There are many small shrines within the precincts of Ogata Shrine. In the past, there used to be two Betsugu shrines and 52 subordinate shrines. One of these shrines, called Hime no Miya, is dedicated to Tamahime no Mikoto (although some people believe it is dedicated to Kurinama no kami). Since ancient times, this shrine has been worshipped as a guardian deity for safe childbirth. This is related to the phallus-shaped object at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} in Komaki City. At the top of Mt. Hongu, there is Hongu Shrine, which is dedicated to the Aramitama of Oogata no Okami. The building of the Ogata Shrine is known as 'Ogata-zukuri' and was constructed in 1661 by {{Ill|Mitsutomo Tokugawa|en}}, ruled the {{ill|Owari Domain|en}} succeeding his father. [http://ooagata.urdr.weblife.me/pg149.html 大縣神社について] In addition to the shrine itself, Ogata Shrine also oversees the [[Aotsuka Kofun]], which is the second largest {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en}} mound in [[Aichi Prefecture]]. The surrounding area is also filled with ancient burial mounds, including round burial mounds. On the slope of the mountain behind the shrine's grounds, there are approximately 300 weeping plum trees. === Architectural Style === The Oagata Shrine holds a place, in the hearts of the people not as a symbol of history and architectural beauty but also as a source of spiritual guidance for those seeking prosperity and protection. Its popularity among both locals and visitors from places highlights its importance as an spiritual hub. By honoring Oagata no okami the shrine maintains its role in the community fostering a connection to tradition and heritage. In essence the Oagata Shrine stands as a landmark that bridges the gap between past and present embodying both the legacy and architectural excellence of the Owari region. Its enduring relevance and the devotion it inspires reflect the impact of Shinto practices, on Japans cultural and religious tapestry. === 1661 restoration === In 1661 Tokugawa Mitsutomo, the lord of the [[Owari Tokugawa Clan]] (rulers of the Owari domain and a cadet branch of the Tokugawa clan, not to be confused with the [[Owari clan]] associated with [[Atsuta Shrine]]) oversaw the reconstruction of the shrine using Santoh zukuri or Ōagata zukuri architectural style. This distinctive construction method is deemed a asset nationally and showcases the unique Owari zukuri architectural heritage. The shrine premises maintain a representation of Owari zukuri aesthetics adding to its cultural significance. It uses {{ill|Owari-zukuri|en}} architecture.https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9696 The shrines existing hall meticulously restored in 1661 by Tokugawa Mitsutomo, the lord of the Owari Domain stands as a testament to the enduring traditions of the Owari region. This restoration work preserved the Owari zukuri building style now esteemed for its historical value. Recognized for its significance and contribution, to Japans heritage the shrine received national recognition as an important cultural property in 1981. Following a restoration led by Tokugawa Mitsutomo in 1661 the shrine boasts architecture reflecting the Owari zukuri construction style.Being recognized as a treasure in 1981 highlights the architectural and historical importance of the shrine preserving a crucial aspect of Japans rich cultural heritage.{{rp|331-353}} === Attractions and Special Sites === The Haiden, known as the Hall of Worship leads to the Honden the shrine recognized as a cultural asset. The shrine grounds also feature an "ema”, for couples seeking blessings for fertility.[[File:Ōagata-jinja_Himeishi.jpg|thumb|293x293px| Himeishi]]The Lady Stone. Hime ishi One striking element at the shrine is the Hime ishi, a stone resembling anatomy located near the Hime no miya shrine. This stone, along with yang stones, at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} collectively known as "in'yoh seki" or yin and yang stones represents fertility and creation. Plum Trees and Hime no miya Shrine [[File:大縣神社 神宮遙拝所 - 1.jpg|thumb|Jingu Yohaijo, or remote worship site for [[Ise Grand Shrine]]]] Surrounded by plum trees the shrine creates a tranquil and scenic atmosphere. Within its premises stands the Hime no miya Shrine dedicated to goddess Tamahime no mikoto. Visitors frequent this site to pray for childbirth, fertility, harmonious relationships and marital bliss. [[File:Small_shrine_of_Oagata-jinja_near_the_top_of_Mount_Hongu_-_3.jpg|thumb|Yama uba Shrine at the top of the mountain]] == Festival == The Hime no Miya Festival, which takes place around the time, as the fertility focused festivities at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} demonstrates the shrines commitment to fertility by honoring both female aspects. This festival, featuring processions and symbols depicting genitalia underscores the shrines connection to the cycles of life and abundance.{{rp|331-353}} The Oagata Shrine festival is sometimes called the Yin Festival, juxaposing it with the Yanf Festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}}. This is because Oagata Shrine celebrates female fertility (yin) and Tagata Shrine celebrates male fertility (yang). The festivities include rituals involving rocks symbolizing anatomy and a procession showcasing a palanquin (mi koshi) designed to resemble female genitalia. Alongside this palanquin visitors can witness banners (nobori) and adorned horses parading around the shrine grounds. A distinctive feature of this festival is the tradition of tossing luck mochi from a palanquin carrying a massive clam. Attendees eagerly gather near the shrine hall to catch these items and other treasures hanging from the sakaki tree. These artifacts are believed to possess powers offering blessings for safe childbirth prosperous marriages and contentment, in marital unions. The Rich Harvest Festival at Ōagata Shrine—also known as Hohnen sai—takes place annually in March. Holds a place, within the local community. The {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} Rich Harvest Festival complements the essence of fertility and abundance symbolizing values through rituals and festivities that attract visitors from all corners of the region. The parallel event held at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} in Komaki City, Aichi Prefecture commemorates the male fertility aspect on the occasion. This celebration is inspired by the tale of Takeinazumi no mikoto, a deity known for his phallus who wed Aratahime no mikoto a revered goddess. The highlight of {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} festivity is the procession featuring a palanquin carrying a linga (representing male genitalia) measuring nearly two meters long. It is followed by youths carrying a banner depicting a phallus. During the festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} attendees eagerly collect fragments of the banner as they believe these pieces hold properties that can ensure crops nurture harmonious relationships and guard against ailments related to intimacy. These fragments are traditionally placed in fields to promote prosperity. Both festivals have roots in customs and are cherished for their emphasis on fertility, abundance and the circle of life. They attract visitors from parts of Japan and beyond providing an enriching glimpse into cultural traditions linked to fertility rituals and reverence, for natural elements. Attending both the Yin festival, at Ōagata Shrine and the Yang festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} is believed to be important for receiving blessings in areas of life and prosperity. These festivals not mark the cycle and human fertility but also have a significant impact, on upholding and spreading local culture and traditions displaying the array of Japanese religious customs and beliefs. == Tourism == The presence of symbols in these shrines can elicit. Shock among foreign visitors a reaction that was more pronounced in earlier times. For instance a foreign traveler in 1970 was taken aback upon encountering symbols for the time, in a popular history magazine detailing these shrines annual festivities. The striking visual representation the banner showcased at the Oagata Festival portraying genitalia vividly illustrates the contrast, in sexual expressions between Japan and Western cultures. The initial shock experienced by travelers in the past has gradually diminished over time suggesting a decreasing disparity in attitudes towards sexuality. This transition is evidenced by the reception of exhibitions in the UK that delve into imagery from times showing a historical Western acceptance of sexual themes similar to contemporary Japanese views. Tourists participate in a variety of customs, such, as purifying themselves at the torii gate walking through a torii to show dedication and making wishes for their desires to be fulfilled. Throughout the years Oagata Shrine and its festivals have adapted to times by blending customs with present day perspectives. While some festival elements have changed or been reimagined to align with views on gender and sexuality the core theme of celebrating fertility and unity remains constant. These adjustments mirror a shift towards recognizing and respecting diverse expressions of human sexuality and fertility within their historical and cultural contexts.{{rp|331-353}} == Directions == To reach Ōagata Shrine ride the Meijo subway line, transfer at Heiandori station to the Kami iida line. The final stop is Gakuden station. From there it's a 1.5 km stroll to the shrine. [[Ukanomitama|Tamahime-no-Mikoto]] (Hime no MIya)|website=http://kikuko-nagoya.com/html/ooagata-shrine.html}} Ōagata Shrine (大縣神社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Inuyama, Aichi, Japan[[Aichi Prefecture|.]] It was recorded in the [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] as a [[Myojin Taisha]]. It is the [[Ninomiya]] or second ranked shrine of [[Owari Province]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]]. It is located next to {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}}. A shrine famous for its Harvest Festival [[Hōnensai]], or the penis festival held annually on March 15.https://www.e-periodica.ch/cntmng?pid=act-001%3A1959%3A16%3A%3A995{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5isFdtMGwVwC&dq=tagata+shrine&pg=PA246|title=Women in Myth|last=Knapp|first=Bettina L.|date=1997-01-01|publisher=SUNY Press|isbn=978-0-7914-3164-1|language=en}} It has a vagina festival on May 14th. Their festival is more subdued.{{Cite web|title=Hime-no-miya Matsuri in Inuyama 犬山の姫の宮祭り by Matthew Haswell|url=https://pbase.com/xerius/himenomiya|access-date=2024-04-08|website=PBase|language=en-US}} They demonstrate religious traditions that starkly contrast with the conventional Western views, on sexuality. With the {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} it is renowned for hosting festivals that prominently showcase sexual symbols showcasing Japans open and accepting attitude towards sexual themes.https://brill.com/previewpdf/book/9789004293786/B9789004293786_003.xml Its name literally means large territory or large [[prefecture]] shrine. The kanji 縣 is the older form of the kanji for prefecture. There are many {{ill|Agata Shrine|ja|縣神社|lt=Agata Shrines}} with the same kanji 縣神社. [[Tagata Shrine]] also has a similar name with the kanji 田 Ta (farm) at the front rather than Great 大 {{clear}} ==Overview== [[File:Oagata1.jpg|thumb| torii gate]] It is the [[Ichinomiya|Ninomiya]], or a second ranked shrine in [[Owari Province]], ranked below {{ill|Masumida Shrine|en}}..{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher=Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} It is located close to {{ill|Tagata Shrine|simple}} the shrine famous for hosting [[Hōnensai]]. Oagata shrine has a similar yonic festival the Sunday before this festival{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2012-03-24 |title=Fertility festival (Oh-agata/ Oagata Jinja) |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2012/03/24/hime-no-miya-festival-ogata-jinja/ |access-date=2023-04-27 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}} [[Aotsuka Kofun]] is located on the grounds of the shrine, 3.5 kilometers to the west of the [[honden]]. The shrine claims that the ''[[kofun]]'' is the grave of its ''[[kami]]'', {{nihongo|Oarata-no-mikoto|大荒田命||}}. During the [[Sengoku period]], the tumulus was fortified as a castle by the forces of [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] during the 1584 {{ill|Battle of Komaki and Nagakute|en}}.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}} {{in lang|ja}} The annual Good Harvest Festival, also known as the Hime no Miya Hōnen Festival is celebrated at Ōagata Shrine, in Inuyama, Aichi, Japan. This special event occurs on nearest Sunday to March 15th each year. Is well known for its emphasis on fertility and prosperity especially representing symbolism. It serves as a celebration to the Good Harvest Festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} creating an observance of fertility with both male and female representations.{{Cite web|date=2008-10-13|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Individual Shrine Observances : Hōnen matsuri|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081013022700/http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=973|access-date=2024-04-08|website=web.archive.org}}{{Cite web|last=Greve|first=Gabi|date=2009-05-15|title=Honen Matsuri Harvest Festival|url=https://wkdfestivalsaijiki.blogspot.com/2009/05/honen-matsuri-harvest-festival.html|access-date=2024-04-08|website=WKD - Saijiki for Festivals and Ceremonies}} The Oagata Shrine, situated in the Owari region holds importance as a Shinto shrine dedicated to Oagata no okami a deity revered for cultivating the Owari area. Known as the prominent shrine, in Owari, Oagata no okami is highly respected as a protective guardian bringing prosperity to businesses and safeguarding against misfortune.{{Cite web|title=Oagata Shrine｜Inuyama Cultural Heritage Navi|url=https://inuyama-tabi.com/en/point/detail/233/|access-date=2024-04-08|website=inuyama-tabi.com}} The Oagata Shrine, located in Inuyama City, within Aichi Prefecture symbolizes Japans traditions by blending ancient customs with modern practices. It is renowned for its festivals that honor fertility and the equilibrium of female energies. Deeply rooted in spirituality this shrine complements the {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} creating a celebration of fertility through their annual events.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=5N8zDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA341&lpg=PA341&dq=%C5%8Cagata+Shrine&source=bl&ots=tWZ72Pe3r1&sig=ACfU3U2PRGcSzIHmkAFq3W8xGUAdo50gcg&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiLgMyErbOFAxUVCTQIHY2HBJE4FBDoAXoECAMQAw#v=onepage&q=%C5%8Cagata%20Shrine&f=false|title=Japan’s Sexual Gods: Shrines, Roles and Rituals of Procreation and Protection|last=Turnbull|first=Stephen|date=2015-05-19|publisher=BRILL|isbn=978-90-04-29378-6|language=en}}{{rp|331-353}} With its history, stunning architecture and distinctive cultural celebrations Oagata Shrine continues to play a role, in Japans spiritual and cultural landscape.{{rp|331-353}} The festivals held at the Oagata Shrine honor the elements of life, fertility and the balance, between female energies. These traditions not uphold Japans heritage but also provide a glimpse into how celebrations have adapted to modern times. The shrines longstanding significance symbolizes the enduring link, between people and spirituality connecting present and future generations.{{rp|331-353}} The Ōagata Shrine stands out as a known Shinto shrine situated in Inuyama, Aichi, Japan, Japan. It pays homage to the revered deity Ōagata oomikami, who is hailed as the trailblazer of the Owari region and a symbol of prosperity and good luck, in business endeavors. Locally referred to as Ninomiya meaning "the shrine " this sacred place holds significance for the community.{{Cite web|title=Kikuko's Website: Oagata Shrine/Honen-sai/|url=http://kikuko-nagoya.com/html/ooagata-shrine.html|access-date=2024-04-08|website=kikuko-nagoya.com}} == deity and Importance == At the heart of Ōagata Shrine lies Ōagata oomikami, honored for their pioneering contributions to Owari and association with prosperity. The shrine serves as a cultural hub in the area drawing visitors seeking blessings for success in business ventures. The shrine claims that the ''[[kofun]]'' is the grave of its ''[[kami]]'', {{nihongo|Oarata-no-mikoto|大荒田命||}}. During the [[Sengoku period]], the tumulus was fortified as a castle by the forces of [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] during the 1584 {{ill|Battle of Komaki and Nagakute|en}}. Enshrining Oagata no okami carries a legacy. Legend has it that the deity was initially enshrined on Mt. Hongu overlooking the Nobi Plain. In a relocation event dating back to 3 BCE, Oagata no okami was transferred to its shrine location solidifying its significance in the local religious context. Dedicated to Oagata no okami a deity associated with the development of the Owari region the Oagata Shrine holds a place as Owaris shrine. It serves as a space where worshippers seek blessings for prosperity and protection from adversity. The shrines history is highlighted by its relocation to its location in 3 BCE from Mt. Hongu showcasing its enduring importance in the communitys beliefs, throughout history.{{rp|331-353}} == Description == [[File:Oagata Shrine Hime no Miya Plum Orchard - 2018.jpg|thumb| Hime no Miya and Umezono]] [[File:Inuyama Oagata Plum Blossoms Over Shrine Rooftops.jpg|thumb| A plum orchard made on a slope.]] There are many small shrines within the precincts of Ogata Shrine. In the past, there used to be two Betsugu shrines and 52 subordinate shrines. One of these shrines, called Hime no Miya, is dedicated to Tamahime no Mikoto (although some people believe it is dedicated to Kurinama no kami). Since ancient times, this shrine has been worshipped as a guardian deity for safe childbirth. This is related to the phallus-shaped object at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} in Komaki City. At the top of Mt. Hongu, there is Hongu Shrine, which is dedicated to the Aramitama of Oogata no Okami. The building of the Ogata Shrine is known as 'Ogata-zukuri' and was constructed in 1661 by {{Ill|Mitsutomo Tokugawa|en}}, ruled the {{ill|Owari Domain|en}} succeeding his father. [http://ooagata.urdr.weblife.me/pg149.html 大縣神社について] In addition to the shrine itself, Ogata Shrine also oversees the [[Aotsuka Kofun]], which is the second largest {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en}} mound in [[Aichi Prefecture]]. The surrounding area is also filled with ancient burial mounds, including round burial mounds. On the slope of the mountain behind the shrine's grounds, there are approximately 300 weeping plum trees. === Architectural Style === The Oagata Shrine holds a place, in the hearts of the people not as a symbol of history and architectural beauty but also as a source of spiritual guidance for those seeking prosperity and protection. Its popularity among both locals and visitors from places highlights its importance as an spiritual hub. By honoring Oagata no okami the shrine maintains its role in the community fostering a connection to tradition and heritage. In essence the Oagata Shrine stands as a landmark that bridges the gap between past and present embodying both the legacy and architectural excellence of the Owari region. Its enduring relevance and the devotion it inspires reflect the impact of Shinto practices, on Japans cultural and religious tapestry. === 1661 restoration === In 1661 Tokugawa Mitsutomo, the lord of the [[Owari Tokugawa Clan]] (rulers of the Owari domain and a cadet branch of the Tokugawa clan, not to be confused with the [[Owari clan]] associated with [[Atsuta Shrine]]) oversaw the reconstruction of the shrine using Santoh zukuri or Ōagata zukuri architectural style. This distinctive construction method is deemed a asset nationally and showcases the unique Owari zukuri architectural heritage. The shrine premises maintain a representation of Owari zukuri aesthetics adding to its cultural significance. It uses {{ill|Owari-zukuri|en}} architecture.https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9696 The shrines existing hall meticulously restored in 1661 by Tokugawa Mitsutomo, the lord of the Owari Domain stands as a testament to the enduring traditions of the Owari region. This restoration work preserved the Owari zukuri building style now esteemed for its historical value. Recognized for its significance and contribution, to Japans heritage the shrine received national recognition as an important cultural property in 1981. Following a restoration led by Tokugawa Mitsutomo in 1661 the shrine boasts architecture reflecting the Owari zukuri construction style.Being recognized as a treasure in 1981 highlights the architectural and historical importance of the shrine preserving a crucial aspect of Japans rich cultural heritage.{{rp|331-353}} === Attractions and Special Sites === The Haiden, known as the Hall of Worship leads to the Honden the shrine recognized as a cultural asset. The shrine grounds also feature an "ema”, for couples seeking blessings for fertility.[[File:Ōagata-jinja_Himeishi.jpg|thumb|293x293px| Himeishi]]The Lady Stone. Hime ishi One striking element at the shrine is the Hime ishi, a stone resembling anatomy located near the Hime no miya shrine. This stone, along with yang stones, at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} collectively known as "in'yoh seki" or yin and yang stones represents fertility and creation. Plum Trees and Hime no miya Shrine [[File:大縣神社 神宮遙拝所 - 1.jpg|thumb|Jingu Yohaijo, or remote worship site for [[Ise Grand Shrine]]]] Surrounded by plum trees the shrine creates a tranquil and scenic atmosphere. Within its premises stands the Hime no miya Shrine dedicated to goddess Tamahime no mikoto. Visitors frequent this site to pray for childbirth, fertility, harmonious relationships and marital bliss. [[File:Small_shrine_of_Oagata-jinja_near_the_top_of_Mount_Hongu_-_3.jpg|thumb|Yama uba Shrine at the top of the mountain]] == Festival == The Hime no Miya Festival, which takes place around the time, as the fertility focused festivities at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} demonstrates the shrines commitment to fertility by honoring both female aspects. This festival, featuring processions and symbols depicting genitalia underscores the shrines connection to the cycles of life and abundance.{{rp|331-353}} The Oagata Shrine festival is sometimes called the Yin Festival, juxaposing it with the Yanf Festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}}. This is because Oagata Shrine celebrates female fertility (yin) and Tagata Shrine celebrates male fertility (yang). The festivities include rituals involving rocks symbolizing anatomy and a procession showcasing a palanquin (mi koshi) designed to resemble female genitalia. Alongside this palanquin visitors can witness banners (nobori) and adorned horses parading around the shrine grounds. A distinctive feature of this festival is the tradition of tossing luck mochi from a palanquin carrying a massive clam. Attendees eagerly gather near the shrine hall to catch these items and other treasures hanging from the sakaki tree. These artifacts are believed to possess powers offering blessings for safe childbirth prosperous marriages and contentment, in marital unions. The Rich Harvest Festival at Ōagata Shrine—also known as Hohnen sai—takes place annually in March. Holds a place, within the local community. The {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} Rich Harvest Festival complements the essence of fertility and abundance symbolizing values through rituals and festivities that attract visitors from all corners of the region. The parallel event held at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} in Komaki City, Aichi Prefecture commemorates the male fertility aspect on the occasion. This celebration is inspired by the tale of Takeinazumi no mikoto, a deity known for his phallus who wed Aratahime no mikoto a revered goddess. The highlight of {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} festivity is the procession featuring a palanquin carrying a linga (representing male genitalia) measuring nearly two meters long. It is followed by youths carrying a banner depicting a phallus. During the festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} attendees eagerly collect fragments of the banner as they believe these pieces hold properties that can ensure crops nurture harmonious relationships and guard against ailments related to intimacy. These fragments are traditionally placed in fields to promote prosperity. Both festivals have roots in customs and are cherished for their emphasis on fertility, abundance and the circle of life. They attract visitors from parts of Japan and beyond providing an enriching glimpse into cultural traditions linked to fertility rituals and reverence, for natural elements. Attending both the Yin festival, at Ōagata Shrine and the Yang festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} is believed to be important for receiving blessings in areas of life and prosperity. These festivals not mark the cycle and human fertility but also have a significant impact, on upholding and spreading local culture and traditions displaying the array of Japanese religious customs and beliefs. == Tourism == The presence of symbols in these shrines can elicit. Shock among foreign visitors a reaction that was more pronounced in earlier times. For instance a foreign traveler in 1970 was taken aback upon encountering symbols for the time, in a popular history magazine detailing these shrines annual festivities. The striking visual representation the banner showcased at the Oagata Festival portraying genitalia vividly illustrates the contrast, in sexual expressions between Japan and Western cultures. The initial shock experienced by travelers in the past has gradually diminished over time suggesting a decreasing disparity in attitudes towards sexuality. This transition is evidenced by the reception of exhibitions in the UK that delve into imagery from times showing a historical Western acceptance of sexual themes similar to contemporary Japanese views. Tourists participate in a variety of customs, such, as purifying themselves at the torii gate walking through a torii to show dedication and making wishes for their desires to be fulfilled. Throughout the years Oagata Shrine and its festivals have adapted to times by blending customs with present day perspectives. While some festival elements have changed or been reimagined to align with views on gender and sexuality the core theme of celebrating fertility and unity remains constant. These adjustments mirror a shift towards recognizing and respecting diverse expressions of human sexuality and fertility within their historical and cultural contexts.{{rp|331-353}} == Directions == To reach Ōagata Shrine ride the Meijo subway line, transfer at Heiandori station to the Kami iida line. The final stop is Gakuden station. From there it's a 1.5 km stroll to the shrine. 社伝によれば「[[垂仁天皇]]27年に、[[本宮山_(犬山市)|本宮山]]の山頂から現在地に移転した」とある。 === 神階 === * [[承和 (日本)|承和]]14年（[[847年]]）[[11月11日]]、無位から従五位下（『[[続日本後紀]]』）- 表記は「大県天神」 * [[仁寿]]3年（[[853年]]）[[5月22日]]、従五位下から従四位下（『[[日本文徳天皇実録]]』）- 表記は「大県神」 * [[天安 (日本)|天安]]3年（[[859年]]）[[2月17日]]、従四位下から従四位上（『[[日本三代実録]]』）- 表記は「大県神」 * [[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]15年（[[873年]]）[[8月13日]]、従四位上から正四位下（『日本三代実録』）- 表記は「大県神」 == 祭神 == 祭神は、大縣大神（おおあがたのおおかみ）としている。大縣大神は、[[国狭槌尊]]とする説、[[天津彦根命]]（大縣主の祖神）とする説、[[少彦名命]]とする説、[[大荒田命]]（[[日本武尊]]の三世孫で迩波縣君の祖）とする説、[[武恵賀前命]]（[[神八井耳命]]の孫で迩波縣君の祖）とする説などがあり、はっきりしない。いずれにしても、「大縣大神は、尾張国開拓の祖神である」とされている。 == 境内 == [[画像:Oagata Shrine Hime no Miya Plum Orchard - 2018.jpg|thumb|姫の宮と梅園]] [[画像:Inuyama Oagata Plum Blossoms Over Shrine Rooftops.jpg|thumb|斜面を利用して作られた梅園。]] [[画像:Ōagata-jinja Himeishi.jpg|thumb|220px|姫石]] 境内には、いくつかの境内社がある。かつては別宮二社、末社52社があったとされる。その中の一つの摂社の姫の宮には、玉姫命が祀られている（[[ウカノミタマ|倉稲魂神]]とする説もある）。ここは古来より安産・子授など女性の守護神として崇敬されており、[[女陰]]をかたどった石などが奉納されている。これは[[小牧市]][[田縣神社]]の[[男根]]に対応するものである。本宮山の山頂には、大縣大神の[[荒魂]]を祀る本宮社がある。 社殿は「大縣造」と称されるもので、[[寛文]]元年([[1661年]])に[[尾張藩]]2代目藩主である[[徳川光友]]によって造営されたものである[http://ooagata.urdr.weblife.me/pg149.html 大縣神社について] 。 また同神社は、愛知県で二番目に大きい前方後円墳である[[青塚古墳 (犬山市)|茶臼山古墳（青塚古墳）]]も管理している。付近には、円墳などの古墳群が点在する。 境内の裏手のある山の斜面には、約300本のしだれ梅の梅園がある。 == 祭事 == === 豊年祭 === 別名「於祖々祭（おそそ祭）」とも言う。毎年[[3月15日]]直前の日曜日に行なわれる祭事。[[女陰]]をかたどった山車などが練り歩く。この祭りと対になっているのが、[[田縣神社|田縣（たがた）神社]]の豊年祭で、こちらでは[[男根]]をかたどった[[神輿]]が練り歩く。 === 梅まつり === 毎年[[3月]]、梅の花が咲く時期に行なわれる祭。[[俳句]]大会なども行なわれる。 == 文化財 == ; 重要文化財 * 大縣神社 2棟 ** 本殿{{Cite web|和書|date= |url=http://www.pref.aichi.jp/kyoiku/bunka/bunkazainavi/yukei/kenzoubutu/kunisitei/0066.html |title=大縣神社本殿祭文殿及び東西回廊 |publisher=愛知県 |accessdate=2013-04-19}}　附透塀1棟、古図1枚、棟札12枚 ** 祭文殿及び東西回廊（1棟）　附棟札1枚 == 施設 == * 総合[[結婚式場]]大縣神社 * 梅園 * 楽田神社 * 大国恵比須神社 == 所在地 == * [[愛知県]][[犬山市]]宮山3 == 交通アクセス == * [[名古屋鉄道|名鉄]][[名鉄小牧線|小牧線]]の[[楽田駅]]下車、徒歩で約20分。または、楽田駅東口から[[犬山市コミュニティバス]] つつじヶ丘団地行き（平日のみ、祝日も運行）で約8分。 * [[愛知県道177号大県神社線]] == 周辺 == === 施設 === * [[老人ホーム]]犬山白寿苑 * 神道祖霊社 * 小西山真長寺 - [[真言宗]][[真言宗醍醐派|醍醐派]]の[[寺院]]。 === その他 === * [[本宮山_(犬山市)|本宮山]] == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * [[鈴木二郎]]『大県神社史』、1969年 == 関連図書 == * 安津素彦・梅田義彦編集兼監修者『神道辞典』[[神社新報]]社、1968年、15頁 * [[白井永二]]・土岐昌訓編集『神社辞典』[[東京堂出版]]、1979年、63頁 == 関連項目 == * [[田縣神社]] - [[愛知県]][[小牧市]]にある神社。大縣神社とは対照的に、「大男茎形（おおおわせがた）」と呼ばれる[[男根]]の形をした御神体が祀られている。毎年3月15日に行なわれる「豊年祭」では、[[男根]]をかたどった[[神輿]]が街を練り歩く。 * [[愛知県道177号大県神社線]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat| Ōagata-jinja}} * [http://ooagata.urdr.weblife.me/ 大縣神社公式HP] * [http://www.kokon.asia/ 古今宗教研究所] ** [http://www.kokon.asia/hokan/ooagata.html 大縣神社] * {{Wayback|url=http://www.geocities.jp/joox_tv2/ |title=トリアゾラムください |date=20190101000000}} ** {{Wayback|url=http://www.geocities.jp/joox_tv2/matsuri/oagata.html |title=大縣神社・豊年祭 |date=20190330042846}} * [https://www.aichi-now.jp/spots/detail/177/　愛知の公式観光ガイド AICHI NOW　大縣神社] {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:おおあかたしんしや}} [[Category:愛知県の神社]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:二宮]] [[Category:尾張国の式内社|名おおあかたしんしや]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:愛知県の重要文化財]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:尾張国|社2]] [[Category:神道と性]] [[Category:性的シンボル]] [[Category:性の文化]] [[Category:江戸時代の建築]] [[Category:犬山市の建築物]] [[Category:犬山市の歴史]]

[[Ukanomitama|Tamahime-no-Mikoto]] (Hime no MIya)|website=http://kikuko-nagoya.com/html/ooagata-shrine.html}} Ōagata Shrine (大縣神社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Inuyama, Aichi, Japan[[Aichi Prefecture|.]] It was recorded in the [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]] as a [[Myojin Taisha]]. It is the [[Ninomiya]] or second ranked shrine of [[Owari Province]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]]. It is located next to {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}}. A shrine famous for its Harvest Festival [[Hōnensai]], or the penis festival held annually on March 15.https://www.e-periodica.ch/cntmng?pid=act-001%3A1959%3A16%3A%3A995{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5isFdtMGwVwC&dq=tagata+shrine&pg=PA246|title=Women in Myth|last=Knapp|first=Bettina L.|date=1997-01-01|publisher=SUNY Press|isbn=978-0-7914-3164-1|language=en}} It has a vagina festival on May 14th. Their festival is more subdued.{{Cite web|title=Hime-no-miya Matsuri in Inuyama 犬山の姫の宮祭り by Matthew Haswell|url=https://pbase.com/xerius/himenomiya|access-date=2024-04-08|website=PBase|language=en-US}} They demonstrate religious traditions that starkly contrast with the conventional Western views, on sexuality. With the {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} it is renowned for hosting festivals that prominently showcase sexual symbols showcasing Japans open and accepting attitude towards sexual themes.https://brill.com/previewpdf/book/9789004293786/B9789004293786_003.xml Its name literally means large territory or large [[prefecture]] shrine. The kanji 縣 is the older form of the kanji for prefecture. There are many {{ill|Agata Shrine|ja|縣神社|lt=Agata Shrines}} with the same kanji 縣神社. [[Tagata Shrine]] also has a similar name with the kanji 田 Ta (farm) at the front rather than Great 大 {{clear}} ==Overview== [[File:Oagata1.jpg|thumb| torii gate]] It is the [[Ichinomiya|Ninomiya]], or a second ranked shrine in [[Owari Province]], ranked below {{ill|Masumida Shrine|en}}..{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher=Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} It is located close to {{ill|Tagata Shrine|simple}} the shrine famous for hosting [[Hōnensai]]. Oagata shrine has a similar yonic festival the Sunday before this festival{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2012-03-24 |title=Fertility festival (Oh-agata/ Oagata Jinja) |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2012/03/24/hime-no-miya-festival-ogata-jinja/ |access-date=2023-04-27 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}} [[Aotsuka Kofun]] is located on the grounds of the shrine, 3.5 kilometers to the west of the [[honden]]. The shrine claims that the ''[[kofun]]'' is the grave of its ''[[kami]]'', {{nihongo|Oarata-no-mikoto|大荒田命||}}. During the [[Sengoku period]], the tumulus was fortified as a castle by the forces of [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] during the 1584 {{ill|Battle of Komaki and Nagakute|en}}.{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}} {{in lang|ja}} The annual Good Harvest Festival, also known as the Hime no Miya Hōnen Festival is celebrated at Ōagata Shrine, in Inuyama, Aichi, Japan. This special event occurs on nearest Sunday to March 15th each year. Is well known for its emphasis on fertility and prosperity especially representing symbolism. It serves as a celebration to the Good Harvest Festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} creating an observance of fertility with both male and female representations.{{Cite web|date=2008-10-13|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto - Home : Individual Shrine Observances : Hōnen matsuri|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081013022700/http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=973|access-date=2024-04-08|website=web.archive.org}}{{Cite web|last=Greve|first=Gabi|date=2009-05-15|title=Honen Matsuri Harvest Festival|url=https://wkdfestivalsaijiki.blogspot.com/2009/05/honen-matsuri-harvest-festival.html|access-date=2024-04-08|website=WKD - Saijiki for Festivals and Ceremonies}} The Oagata Shrine, situated in the Owari region holds importance as a Shinto shrine dedicated to Oagata no okami a deity revered for cultivating the Owari area. Known as the prominent shrine, in Owari, Oagata no okami is highly respected as a protective guardian bringing prosperity to businesses and safeguarding against misfortune.{{Cite web|title=Oagata Shrine｜Inuyama Cultural Heritage Navi|url=https://inuyama-tabi.com/en/point/detail/233/|access-date=2024-04-08|website=inuyama-tabi.com}} The Oagata Shrine, located in Inuyama City, within Aichi Prefecture symbolizes Japans traditions by blending ancient customs with modern practices. It is renowned for its festivals that honor fertility and the equilibrium of female energies. Deeply rooted in spirituality this shrine complements the {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} creating a celebration of fertility through their annual events.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=5N8zDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA341&lpg=PA341&dq=%C5%8Cagata+Shrine&source=bl&ots=tWZ72Pe3r1&sig=ACfU3U2PRGcSzIHmkAFq3W8xGUAdo50gcg&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiLgMyErbOFAxUVCTQIHY2HBJE4FBDoAXoECAMQAw#v=onepage&q=%C5%8Cagata%20Shrine&f=false|title=Japan’s Sexual Gods: Shrines, Roles and Rituals of Procreation and Protection|last=Turnbull|first=Stephen|date=2015-05-19|publisher=BRILL|isbn=978-90-04-29378-6|language=en}}{{rp|331-353}} With its history, stunning architecture and distinctive cultural celebrations Oagata Shrine continues to play a role, in Japans spiritual and cultural landscape.{{rp|331-353}} The festivals held at the Oagata Shrine honor the elements of life, fertility and the balance, between female energies. These traditions not uphold Japans heritage but also provide a glimpse into how celebrations have adapted to modern times. The shrines longstanding significance symbolizes the enduring link, between people and spirituality connecting present and future generations.{{rp|331-353}} The Ōagata Shrine stands out as a known Shinto shrine situated in Inuyama, Aichi, Japan, Japan. It pays homage to the revered deity Ōagata oomikami, who is hailed as the trailblazer of the Owari region and a symbol of prosperity and good luck, in business endeavors. Locally referred to as Ninomiya meaning "the shrine " this sacred place holds significance for the community.{{Cite web|title=Kikuko's Website: Oagata Shrine/Honen-sai/|url=http://kikuko-nagoya.com/html/ooagata-shrine.html|access-date=2024-04-08|website=kikuko-nagoya.com}} == deity and Importance == At the heart of Ōagata Shrine lies Ōagata oomikami, honored for their pioneering contributions to Owari and association with prosperity. The shrine serves as a cultural hub in the area drawing visitors seeking blessings for success in business ventures. The shrine claims that the ''[[kofun]]'' is the grave of its ''[[kami]]'', {{nihongo|Oarata-no-mikoto|大荒田命||}}. During the [[Sengoku period]], the tumulus was fortified as a castle by the forces of [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi]] during the 1584 {{ill|Battle of Komaki and Nagakute|en}}. Enshrining Oagata no okami carries a legacy. Legend has it that the deity was initially enshrined on Mt. Hongu overlooking the Nobi Plain. In a relocation event dating back to 3 BCE, Oagata no okami was transferred to its shrine location solidifying its significance in the local religious context. Dedicated to Oagata no okami a deity associated with the development of the Owari region the Oagata Shrine holds a place as Owaris shrine. It serves as a space where worshippers seek blessings for prosperity and protection from adversity. The shrines history is highlighted by its relocation to its location in 3 BCE from Mt. Hongu showcasing its enduring importance in the communitys beliefs, throughout history.{{rp|331-353}} == Description == [[File:Oagata Shrine Hime no Miya Plum Orchard - 2018.jpg|thumb| Hime no Miya and Umezono]] [[File:Inuyama Oagata Plum Blossoms Over Shrine Rooftops.jpg|thumb| A plum orchard made on a slope.]] There are many small shrines within the precincts of Ogata Shrine. In the past, there used to be two Betsugu shrines and 52 subordinate shrines. One of these shrines, called Hime no Miya, is dedicated to Tamahime no Mikoto (although some people believe it is dedicated to Kurinama no kami). Since ancient times, this shrine has been worshipped as a guardian deity for safe childbirth. This is related to the phallus-shaped object at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} in Komaki City. At the top of Mt. Hongu, there is Hongu Shrine, which is dedicated to the Aramitama of Oogata no Okami. The building of the Ogata Shrine is known as 'Ogata-zukuri' and was constructed in 1661 by {{Ill|Mitsutomo Tokugawa|en}}, ruled the {{ill|Owari Domain|en}} succeeding his father. [http://ooagata.urdr.weblife.me/pg149.html 大縣神社について] In addition to the shrine itself, Ogata Shrine also oversees the [[Aotsuka Kofun]], which is the second largest {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en}} mound in [[Aichi Prefecture]]. The surrounding area is also filled with ancient burial mounds, including round burial mounds. On the slope of the mountain behind the shrine's grounds, there are approximately 300 weeping plum trees. === Architectural Style === The Oagata Shrine holds a place, in the hearts of the people not as a symbol of history and architectural beauty but also as a source of spiritual guidance for those seeking prosperity and protection. Its popularity among both locals and visitors from places highlights its importance as an spiritual hub. By honoring Oagata no okami the shrine maintains its role in the community fostering a connection to tradition and heritage. In essence the Oagata Shrine stands as a landmark that bridges the gap between past and present embodying both the legacy and architectural excellence of the Owari region. Its enduring relevance and the devotion it inspires reflect the impact of Shinto practices, on Japans cultural and religious tapestry. === 1661 restoration === In 1661 Tokugawa Mitsutomo, the lord of the [[Owari Tokugawa Clan]] (rulers of the Owari domain and a cadet branch of the Tokugawa clan, not to be confused with the [[Owari clan]] associated with [[Atsuta Shrine]]) oversaw the reconstruction of the shrine using Santoh zukuri or Ōagata zukuri architectural style. This distinctive construction method is deemed a asset nationally and showcases the unique Owari zukuri architectural heritage. The shrine premises maintain a representation of Owari zukuri aesthetics adding to its cultural significance. It uses {{ill|Owari-zukuri|en}} architecture.https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9696 The shrines existing hall meticulously restored in 1661 by Tokugawa Mitsutomo, the lord of the Owari Domain stands as a testament to the enduring traditions of the Owari region. This restoration work preserved the Owari zukuri building style now esteemed for its historical value. Recognized for its significance and contribution, to Japans heritage the shrine received national recognition as an important cultural property in 1981. Following a restoration led by Tokugawa Mitsutomo in 1661 the shrine boasts architecture reflecting the Owari zukuri construction style.Being recognized as a treasure in 1981 highlights the architectural and historical importance of the shrine preserving a crucial aspect of Japans rich cultural heritage.{{rp|331-353}} === Attractions and Special Sites === The Haiden, known as the Hall of Worship leads to the Honden the shrine recognized as a cultural asset. The shrine grounds also feature an "ema”, for couples seeking blessings for fertility.[[File:Ōagata-jinja_Himeishi.jpg|thumb|293x293px| Himeishi]]The Lady Stone. Hime ishi One striking element at the shrine is the Hime ishi, a stone resembling anatomy located near the Hime no miya shrine. This stone, along with yang stones, at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} collectively known as "in'yoh seki" or yin and yang stones represents fertility and creation. Plum Trees and Hime no miya Shrine [[File:大縣神社 神宮遙拝所 - 1.jpg|thumb|Jingu Yohaijo, or remote worship site for [[Ise Grand Shrine]]]] Surrounded by plum trees the shrine creates a tranquil and scenic atmosphere. Within its premises stands the Hime no miya Shrine dedicated to goddess Tamahime no mikoto. Visitors frequent this site to pray for childbirth, fertility, harmonious relationships and marital bliss. [[File:Small_shrine_of_Oagata-jinja_near_the_top_of_Mount_Hongu_-_3.jpg|thumb|Yama uba Shrine at the top of the mountain]] == Festival == The Hime no Miya Festival, which takes place around the time, as the fertility focused festivities at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} demonstrates the shrines commitment to fertility by honoring both female aspects. This festival, featuring processions and symbols depicting genitalia underscores the shrines connection to the cycles of life and abundance.{{rp|331-353}} The Oagata Shrine festival is sometimes called the Yin Festival, juxaposing it with the Yanf Festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}}. This is because Oagata Shrine celebrates female fertility (yin) and Tagata Shrine celebrates male fertility (yang). The festivities include rituals involving rocks symbolizing anatomy and a procession showcasing a palanquin (mi koshi) designed to resemble female genitalia. Alongside this palanquin visitors can witness banners (nobori) and adorned horses parading around the shrine grounds. A distinctive feature of this festival is the tradition of tossing luck mochi from a palanquin carrying a massive clam. Attendees eagerly gather near the shrine hall to catch these items and other treasures hanging from the sakaki tree. These artifacts are believed to possess powers offering blessings for safe childbirth prosperous marriages and contentment, in marital unions. The Rich Harvest Festival at Ōagata Shrine—also known as Hohnen sai—takes place annually in March. Holds a place, within the local community. The {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} Rich Harvest Festival complements the essence of fertility and abundance symbolizing values through rituals and festivities that attract visitors from all corners of the region. The parallel event held at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} in Komaki City, Aichi Prefecture commemorates the male fertility aspect on the occasion. This celebration is inspired by the tale of Takeinazumi no mikoto, a deity known for his phallus who wed Aratahime no mikoto a revered goddess. The highlight of {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} festivity is the procession featuring a palanquin carrying a linga (representing male genitalia) measuring nearly two meters long. It is followed by youths carrying a banner depicting a phallus. During the festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} attendees eagerly collect fragments of the banner as they believe these pieces hold properties that can ensure crops nurture harmonious relationships and guard against ailments related to intimacy. These fragments are traditionally placed in fields to promote prosperity. Both festivals have roots in customs and are cherished for their emphasis on fertility, abundance and the circle of life. They attract visitors from parts of Japan and beyond providing an enriching glimpse into cultural traditions linked to fertility rituals and reverence, for natural elements. Attending both the Yin festival, at Ōagata Shrine and the Yang festival at {{ill|Tagata Shrine|en|Tagata Shrine|fr|Tagata-jinja}} is believed to be important for receiving blessings in areas of life and prosperity. These festivals not mark the cycle and human fertility but also have a significant impact, on upholding and spreading local culture and traditions displaying the array of Japanese religious customs and beliefs. == Tourism == The presence of symbols in these shrines can elicit. Shock among foreign visitors a reaction that was more pronounced in earlier times. For instance a foreign traveler in 1970 was taken aback upon encountering symbols for the time, in a popular history magazine detailing these shrines annual festivities. The striking visual representation the banner showcased at the Oagata Festival portraying genitalia vividly illustrates the contrast, in sexual expressions between Japan and Western cultures. The initial shock experienced by travelers in the past has gradually diminished over time suggesting a decreasing disparity in attitudes towards sexuality. This transition is evidenced by the reception of exhibitions in the UK that delve into imagery from times showing a historical Western acceptance of sexual themes similar to contemporary Japanese views. Tourists participate in a variety of customs, such, as purifying themselves at the torii gate walking through a torii to show dedication and making wishes for their desires to be fulfilled. Throughout the years Oagata Shrine and its festivals have adapted to times by blending customs with present day perspectives. While some festival elements have changed or been reimagined to align with views on gender and sexuality the core theme of celebrating fertility and unity remains constant. These adjustments mirror a shift towards recognizing and respecting diverse expressions of human sexuality and fertility within their historical and cultural contexts.{{rp|331-353}} == Directions == To reach Ōagata Shrine ride the Meijo subway line, transfer at Heiandori station to the Kami iida line. The final stop is Gakuden station. From there it's a 1.5 km stroll to the shrine.
